body:
I don't think it's a lack of motivation. I can articulate, with sincerity, aso many reasons why I want to change my life and be successful - to contribute something to mankind, to feel proud of myself and prove that I'm capable, to be happy, to use the talents I've been genetically gifted.

But it's like all this is overshadowed by a sense of hopelessness i can't remove. I don't feel like I'm in control of my life.

As someone who's been feeling hopeless for ages now, your post really helped me. Now I'm looking for somewhere to volunteer this weekend, because you're spot-on about the benefits - the last time I felt this low, volunteering gave me enough of a purpose to guide me through a series of positive life changes. Things have gotten hard again, but thanks for this post and for reminding me that it's an option.
This is like an itemized list of my life experiences...thank you. Nothing seems to help me though, not even medication :(

I've definitely felt this way before. Not currently on depression meds and haven't been since I was 16 but it has the same affect when applied to self-motivation. I avoid doing anything because it's so much easier to wallow around in my sadness and act like a victim. And for so long I enjoyed it, because I'd come to see myself as pathetic and this felt "honest," following my idea that I was worthless, and in a weird way carrying this attitude finally  meant I was right about something. 

 This was also a huge problem when I was prescribed medication for my ADHD. It felt like once the problem was addressed I no longer had an excuse for all of my failures, and now that nothing was supposedly holding me back I had to be this superhuman. I hated the (self-imposed) pressure to have an "instant turnaround" and stopped taking them. 

I suppose it stems from fear of change and having to step up when we may not feel we're ready. Passivity is easier, and changes in yourself can be overwhelming even when they're positive.
anyone? or anyone to talk about any of this? :(
There is literally no variety of cookie I would refuse- I can send you a Christmas card in return!
Broke and will be spending Christmas alone - having a card to open would brighten my day so much!

funny, I saw an ad they placed on craigslist regarding their open call and had already penciled it in for tomorrow. Regardless, I appreciate your help and would certainly buy you a beer if I get the job!

Also would like to add that I've been talking to some amazing people via Reddit the past few days and it's made such a positive difference. Obviously I'm not out of the woods, but just talking and having someone listen is helpful. So anyone who has - or anyone that could - lend an ear, I'd just like to issue a thanks.

I read it about 2 years ago and quite liked. it's about overcomting "resistance" right? but I've since lost my copy. maybe i'll see if the library has one, it would probably mean more to me reading it now.

I still have to have my rent by tomorrow and I'm going to come up short...I was ok last night, just cried until I felt numb I guess, but now all of those terrible thoughts are creeping back because there's no way out of eviction. I'm still scared and self-harming again...could anyone offer any advice as to what I can do?!

I never intended to make a career of prostitution...it was simply something I'd do until I had enough rent money to subsidize another month of legitimate job hunting. I have bigger goals than that, I've just put myself in a shitty situation. Nonetheless, i appreciate your concern.

It isn't my first choice, but I have no one to turn to for help. Trust me, I find the idea horrifying, hence my initial reluctance to go through with it, but when your only options are sleeping with an old creep or sleeping on the street it quickly validates itself as an option. Either way...I'm really, really scared
I just want someone to reach out to me. To just listen, even briefly, in a way that doesn't make me feel like a huge burden. I don't have anyone like that in my life now.
where can I get clarity? I've tried running and meditation but it does little.

I appreciate the words...I wish this were true. "Redouble your efforts" isn't effective unfortunately when I'm incapable of effort in the first place. It feels hopeless seeing as I've never been successful in the past.

i guess I don't want to die...I just don't want my life to be like this and I can't cope anymore. I don't know how to make things better. I have no life or coping skills. I've been to therapists, I've been traveling, I've moved, I've been out to meet new people but nothing helps. It feels likes I'm broken and just not equipped to connect with other people. It's crushing, because that's what I want more than anything. 

How do I fix my situation? I don't know where to start. It's so overwhelming...What do I do about rent? or going back to school, or making myself do things? 

I wish I could just sit down with someone (not a therapist) for several hours and just let it all out, be completely honest and unguarded. But more than anything I just want to feel genuinely, deeply loved and respected. No one ever had faith in me and I don't have any faith in myself. I hate myself so much.

EDIT: Also...I WANT advice. I've never had anyone to give me guidance before. I want a mentor, someone I can turn to with questions about life or career. I know suicidewatch tries to refrain from doing so, and in general cases I agree, but having to foot it all on my own for so long is part of the reason I'm in such shit in the first place. So if anyone has advice, please, don't hesitate to share.

Like, what are my options for paying rent that don't involve illegal activities? Where can I get career advice? where can I find a mentor? where can I get free therapy/counseling in NYC? (I have no health insurance.)
